correctness.reasoning: The width of a confidence interval is determined by its margin of error. To make a confidence interval shorter (narrower), you must decrease the margin of error. The margin of error is proportional to the critical value (which is determined by the confidence level) and inversely proportional to the square root of the sample size. Decreasing the confidence level produces a smaller critical value, which narrows the interval. Increasing the sample size produces a smaller standard error, which also narrows the interval.
